title: Crêpes
summary: Thin, flexible egg-based crêpes held together with a little psyllium, for folding around sweet or savoury fillings.

ingredients.note: melted, plus extra for the pan

steps: Blend all the ingredients until completely smooth, about 30 seconds.
Let the batter rest 10 minutes so the psyllium and coconut flour hydrate; it should be like thin cream. Add a spoonful of water if it is thicker.
Heat a 20 cm (8 in) non-stick pan over medium heat and brush with butter.
Pour in 3 tablespoons of batter and swirl at once to coat the base thinly.
Cook about 1 minute, until the edge lifts and the underside is lightly golden. Loosen with a thin spatula, flip and cook 20–30 seconds more.
Stack on a plate and repeat, stirring the batter each time.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free butter gives slightly paler crêpes but the texture is the same.
tips: Fill with whipped cream and a few berries, or with ham and spinach for a savoury version.

origin.history: Brittany is the home of the crêpe. Buckwheat, which grows on poor soil, spread there in the late Middle Ages, and thin buckwheat galettes became a staple; sweeter wheat crêpes followed as white flour became affordable. Crêperies carried the dish across France and beyond.
